correctness.rationale: At a union node, independent uniform relative orders on the child vertex sets make the greedy output law a product distribution, and maximal independent sets decompose uniquely across all children. At a join node, the child containing the globally earliest vertex is selected with probability \(n_i/n\); all other children are then blocked, and conditional on that selection the relative order inside the chosen child remains uniform. This proves the exact law. Uniformity follows by comparing individual maximal-independent-set probabilities, giving the necessary and sufficient equal-ratio condition \(n_i/m_i=n_j/m_j\) at every join. The induction covers every finite cograph. The bundled exact checker independently verifies the law on all \(6039\) labeled cographs through order \(6\), totaling \(4020821\) vertex permutations.

originality.rationale: The initiating 2026 tree paper studies exactly the same random-order greedy terminal law, proves rigidity on trees, and identifies classification beyond trees as an open direction. Full-text inspection found no cograph theorem there. Focused published-finding corpus searches under cograph/cotree, join/union, permutation-fibre, exact-law, and uniformity formulations returned threshold-graph, chain-graph, and complete-multipartite results as the closest records, but none implies an exact recursive law or uniformity classification for all cographs. Classical cograph sources supply the cotree decomposition only. The main residual risk is that this natural recursion may exist implicitly or folklorically under modular-decomposition terminology.
residual_risks: Because the union/join rules are structurally natural, an equivalent cograph theorem may exist as an implicit or poorly indexed observation in modular-decomposition or random-priority literature.

The classical cograph source was available at abstract/structural-description level rather than as full article text; it is not itself a plausible stochastic covering source, but terminology from older cograph literature may differ.

value.rationale: The initiating paper explicitly motivates classification of exact greedy uniformity beyond trees. Cographs are a canonical hereditary class with a unique cotree and include substantial families such as threshold and complete multipartite graphs. The result gives the complete output law, not merely an expectation or one optimum, and converts exact uniformity into a bottom-up structural criterion that avoids maximal-independent-set enumeration. This is a natural full-class classification with reusable join/union structure rather than an arbitrary finite slice or parameter substitution.
